## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I** – Impl: idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget (browse.ts) (completed)
- **WL-0MPFFGIPX007B87F** – [test-failure] prints per-item synced list when --verbose is provided — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 60s, acceptance, aligned, already, auto (+82 more)
- `scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 60s, acceptance, already, approach, args (+81 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: adding, already, auto, bug, caller (+64 more)


---

## Plan (WL-0MSJNJXX2001NMHS — planning complete 2026-08-23)

### Features (children)

1. **Tests: hung wl refresh resolves via timeout; next tick proceeds** — `WL-0MT60Q89I003KRMJ` (task, test-first). Unit tests proving every refresh/sync-path `runWl` caller passes a bounded timeout when no override is given; claim's 3000ms override survives; `checkWlAvailable` probe bounded; a hung execFile (mock honoring `options.timeout` under fake timers) rejects after the timeout; worklist-level: `Refresh failed` toast, guard cleared, next tick refreshes.
2. **Impl: default bounded wl spawn timeout in fetcher (DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS)** — `WL-0MT60Q86F003QNIS` (task). `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` default inside `runWl`/`runWlInner` when caller omits; per-call overrides (`CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS=3000`) preserved; graceful failure path (toast + guard cleared + next tick retries).
3. **Impl: bound wl --version probe in checkWlAvailable** — `WL-0MT60Q7ZP0000AXZ` (task). Ninety-second-class fix: `wl --version` startup probe passes `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`; timeout → returns false (fail-open unchanged).

### Dependencies

- Impl #2 → depends on Tests #1 (test-first)
- Impl #3 → depends on Tests #1 (test-first)

### Decisions approved by producer (2026-08-23, "all as recommended")

- **Q1 — Timeout value:** fixed `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, aligned with auto-sync's existing 60s spawn safety timeout and the pi extension convention (auto-sync.ts:227). Not env-configurable.
- **Q2 — Scope:** also bound the `checkWlAvailable` startup probe (`wl --version`, fetcher.ts:421).
- **Q3 — Adjacent wedge:** `herdr agent list` inside `doRefresh` (agent-tracker.ts:208) is out of scope (AC-1 is wl-specific); follow-up work item to be filed separately.

### Notes

- The description's "single fix closes both" note is stale: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (downtime worker hung exec) is already completed — index.ts uses `DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS=10_000`. This item covers only the herdr refresh/sync fetch path + the version probe.

- Risk: **Medium** (10/25) — mitigations: targeted tests, compatibility tests, extra review.
- Confidence: 76%.

- **Q1 (asked by plan, 2026-08-23):** "Q1 — Timeout value. AC allows 30–60s 'configurable or aligned with existing constants'. Recommend: fixed `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (matches auto-sync's 60s and the pi extension convention named in auto-sync.ts:227), exported from fetcher.ts, per-call override retained. 60s fixed (recommended) · 30s · env-configurable `WL_TIMEOUT_MS`?"

Include? Yes, bound it (recommended) · No, strictly refresh/sync fetch path?"
  **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23):** "all as recommended" → final: **yes, bound the probe too**. Evidence: fetcher.ts:421 (unbounded execFileAsync), index.ts:952 (await at startup).
- **Q3 (asked by plan, 2026-08-23):** "Q3 — Adjacent wedge: `herdr agent list` awaited inside `doRefresh` (agent-tracker.ts:208) with no timeout — a hung `herdr` (not `wl`) would wedge the same guard. Out of AC scope (AC-1 says 'wl spawn'). Out of scope, file a follow-up (recommended) · Fold into this item · Ignore?"
  **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23):** "all as recommended" → final: **out of scope; file a follow-up work item** (to be created separately with `discovered-from: WL-0MSJNJXX2001NMHS`). Evidence: agent-tracker.ts:208 `execFileAsync(bin, ['agent', 'list'], { maxBuffer })` — no timeout.

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Compress the space used in herdr plugin meta-data

## Problem Statement

The metadata section in the herdr plugin's list-mode metadata panel and detail view
occupies too much vertical space. Key related fields are displayed on separate rows
when they could be compacted, wasting limited terminal real estate.

## Users

- **Terminal users viewing work items** — want to see more metadata at a glance without
  scrolling through verbose, line-by-line display.
- **Users with limited terminal height** — benefit from denser metadata presentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Status + Stage** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Status+Stage: 🔄 in_progress / 🛠️ in_progress` (or similar compact format).
2. **Priority + Type** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Priority+Type: ⭐ high / feature`.
3. **Created + Updated** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Created+Updated: 01/08/26 10:00 / 02/08/26 10:00`.
4. **Audit + Audited At** are displayed on the same row, e.g. `Audit+AuditedAt: ✅ ready to close / 03/08/26 10:00`.
5. The detail view metadata table is also compressed consistently (the same field pairings).
6. All other metadata rows (ID, Title, Risk, Effort, Children, Parent, Tags, GitHub Issue, Reviewed) remain unchanged.
7. Full project test suite passes with changes.

## Constraints

- Existing field labels and icon behavior must be preserved (no changes to icon mapping).
- The compact format should be readable — avoid over-compression that harms scannability.
- No changes to the `WorkItem` type or data model — purely a display change.
- `noIcons` mode (plain text) must also be handled correctly for compacted rows.

## Existing State

- `buildMetaRows()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` returns an array of `[label, value]` pairs, one per row.
- `formatMetadataPanel()` renders each pair as a separate line: `  <label padded> <value>`.
- `formatDetailContent()` similarly renders the detail view table.
- Key files:
  - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildMetaRows()`, `formatMetadataPanel()`, `formatDetailContent()`
  - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for metadata row building and formatting

## Desired Change

Introduce paired-row rendering for the four specified field pairs. Options considered:

1. **Change `buildMetaRows` to emit compound rows** — modify the data structure to return
   pairs-of-pairs for the four groupings, then update rendering.
2. **Keep `buildMetaRows` unchanged, introduce a post-processing step** — leave the row
   data intact but compress during rendering in `formatMetadataPanel` and `formatDetailContent`.

**Recommendation:** Option 2 — less invasive, keeps `buildMetaRows` as the single source
of truth for field data, and localizes the rendering logic change.

## Related Work

- WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9 — Icon + text metadata values (ensures icon handling is consistent).
- WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J — Dynamic metadata panel sizing.
- WL-0MSEPP0MB009K9PR — Responsive metadata panel layout implementation.
- WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7 — Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section.

# Intake Brief: Sync — Regression Guard

## Problem Statement

When `wl sync` merges remote state that is newer than local, it can silently import regressions: fields the local store had set to non-default values (e.g. `effort: 'Small'`, `status: completed`) get overwritten with defaults by a stale/divergent second store, as observed Aug 6–10, 2026 on the llm worklog ref.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators of multi-store worklog setups — anyone running more than one `wl sync` instance against the same remote.
- **Secondary**: Producers/reviewers whose audit results (status/stage transitions) are silently reverted by stale syncs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During merge, for each incoming remote item with a newer `updatedAt` than local, detect regressions where a field moves from a non-default value to its default on the fields that participate in the merge: `status`/`stage` (non-default → default, e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/idea`), `priority` (non-default → default), and `assignee` (set → unset).

   **`effort`/`risk` (producer resolution, 2026-08-23): stay PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the merge field lists** — ping-pong prevention by construction. A remote `effort: ''` / `risk: ''` never enters the merge; local non-default values are always kept. The guard additionally REPORTS any attempted effort/risk regression (remote non-empty → default) as a protected conflict (local kept, nothing imported) for observability, but no override path is needed for these two fields since they cannot be imported through the merge.
2. On detecting a regression, `wl sync` refuses to import that item's regressed fields: reports the conflict (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value) and keeps the local value. An explicit override flag (`--accept-regressions` or equivalent) allows the operator to accept the regression.
3. Genuine concurrent edits (both stores changed different non-default fields, or both changed the same field to different non-default values) still merge and re-timestamp exactly as today — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution.
4. The regression guard applies only to the `import()`/merge path used by `wl sync` — it does NOT affect explicit user `wl update` commands, which remain authoritative.
5. Unit tests cover: (a) newer remote with `effort: ''` against local `effort: 'Small'` → local kept (exclusion by construction), conflict REPORTED as protected, remote value NOT imported; (b) newer remote with `status: open` against local `completed` → refused, local kept, conflict reported; (c) both sides non-default differing → normal merge + re-timestamp (no regression path — guard must NOT alter legitimate conflict resolution); (d) override flag accepts the regression for merge-participating fields only; (e) `--dry-run` reports the same refusals.
6. Manual verification: sync against the known commit `5fc880a` (effort/risk cleared) → regressions refused and reported; sync against `54b1375` (restored values) → no regression flags.

## Constraints

- Must not change behavior for legitimate concurrent edits — the guard is regression-only, not conflict-resolution.
- Must be deterministic: dry-run and normal sync report the same refusals.
- Does NOT prevent a second store from pushing — it prevents the primary store from absorbing regressive state.
- Complements the identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) — the identity gate catches the writer; this guard catches the damage even if the writer's identity is unknown.

## Existing State

The merge functions (`mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` in `src/sync.ts`) already implement a non-default-preference heuristic: when one side has a non-default value and the other has a default, the non-default is preserved. The `isDefaultValue` helper in `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` classifies empty strings, `undefined`, and empty arrays as defaults.

The merge field arrays include `status`, `stage`, `priority`, and `assignee` — these fields **already** keep the local non-default value when the remote sends a default (via the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch). They do **not** produce an explicit regression report — the local value is silently kept.

The merge field arrays do **not** include `effort` or `risk` — these fields are never merged at all; the local value is always preserved regardless of the remote.

**Contradiction — RESOLVED (producer decision, 2026-08-23)**: The 13-field merge list currently excludes `effort`/`risk` (code-confirmed), yet the original ACs listed them as regression targets. Producer directive: *"The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to."* Resolution: **Reading A** — `effort`/`risk` remain excluded from the merge lists; adding them to the merge would re-introduce the ping-pong (the DB re-timestamp amplifier in `hasWorkItemChanged` already tracks these fields, so a single unguarded import becomes the newest record and propagates). The guard therefore targets the merge-participating fields (`status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`), and `effort`/`risk` regressions are reported as protected (local kept). Effort/risk merge-participation is a non-goal.

## Desired Change

Add a regression detection layer on top of the merge path that:
- Identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in newer remote state, for the merge-participating fields: `status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`
- Reports conflicts with details (item id, field, old value, new value)
- Refuses to import regressed fields (keeping local) unless overridden (`--accept-regressions`, merge-participating fields only)
- Preserves all existing merge behavior for non-regression cases
- Reports (without importing) attempted `effort`/`risk` regressions as protected — these fields remain excluded from the merge lists (non-goal: adding them back)

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regression detection logic breaks existing merge behavior | High | Unit tests must verify non-regression cases still merge correctly (AC3) |
| Scope creep: "regression" definition might be too broad (e.g., should a valid transition like `in_progress → open` count as regression?) | Medium | Strict definition: only non-default → default transitions count |
| Override flag (`--accept-regressions`) could be misused, allowing silent data loss | Medium | Require explicit flag; report what was accepted in output |
| **DECIDED**: effort/risk must NOT be added to the merge list | — | Producer resolution 2026-08-23: adding them re-introduces ping-pong (DB re-timestamp amplifier `hasWorkItemChanged` tracks these fields; one unguarded import becomes the newest record) |
| `isDefaultValue` may not correctly identify defaults for all fields (e.g., custom stages) | Low | Only built-in defaults (`open`, `idea`, `medium`, empty strings) are guarded; custom stages fall through to normal merge |
| **Scope-creep risk**: The guard could be extended to "merge strategies" or general conflict-policy work — those are separate concerns. | Medium | Record as future work items; do not implement here |

**Assumptions**:
- The `isDefaultValue` function correctly classifies all default values for the fields in question
- Regression detection can be cleanly layered on top of existing merge logic without restructuring
- The operator will accept a new CLI flag for override

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection alongside the existing merge logic (field lists UNCHANGED for `effort`/`risk` — exclusion is the ping-pong prevention)
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes (already classifies empties as defaults)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — CLI flag for `--accept-regressions`, conflict reporting in output
- `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — new test file for regression detection scenarios

## Related Work

| ID | Title | Relationship |
|----|-------|-------------|
| WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB | Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits | Related: same root cause incident (Aug 2026 llm worklog pollution); identity gate catches the writer, regression guard catches the damage |
| WL-0MSORD6HC005QVZX | Sync: do not change updatedAt on whitespace-only changes | Completed; orthogonal concern |
| WL-0MKVZ510K1XHJ7B3 | Sync & data integrity | Completed; foundational sync merge logic |
| WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH | Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence | Completed; identity gate now wired into sync |

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q (auto-resolved by code inspection)**: The description says "the 13-field merge list currently excludes effort/risk" — the code confirms `effort` and `risk` are NOT in the merge field arrays. Does this mean: (a) the ACs about effort/risk are stale and should be removed, or (b) the description is outdated and effort/risk regressions need explicit detection and reporting? → **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23): "The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to." Interpreted as Reading A: effort/risk stay excluded from the merge lists (prevention by construction); the guard targets merge-participating fields (status/stage/priority/assignee) and reports protected effort/risk conflict attempts without importing them. Adding effort/risk to the merge is a non-goal.** Source: interactive reply, this intake session (2026-08-23).
- **Q**: What is the exact override flag name? The ACs mention `--accept-regressions` or equivalent. → **Flagged for producer confirmation.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS8XLS0Z00759QI** – Pi TUI tools.ts: smart selection (helper copy + fetch merge + apply) (completed)
- **WL-0MSVRMAWM007QNR5** – Downtime worker: parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id — every poll fail-closes to busy, zero dispatches (completed)
- **WL-0MSHWHFAK005WKDB** – [test-failure] defaultSettings has default browseItemCount of 10 — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+231 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+204 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, accepts, add, adding, affect (+191 more)

## Problem

`prefix+l` in herdr (→ `worklog-selection-list.open-podcast-editor-tab`) crashed immediately: the spawned worklist pane exited with code 1 within ~0.3s.

## Root cause

The pane runs `npx tsx src/index.ts`; the plugin crashed on startup with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'marked' imported from .../packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts
```

`marked` (and the `@worklog/shared` file dependency) are declared in `packages/herdr/package.json` but were not installed. The root `npm run build` postbuild hook (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) links the plugin and registers the prefix+l keybinding but never runs `npm install`, so a fresh clone (or a node_modules cleanup) leaves the plugin broken with a confusing 'crash on prefix+l' symptom.

## Fix

Ensure dependencies are installed as part of the plugin build. Options:
- Run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) in `packages/herdr` inside the `[[build]]` step or the root postbuild hook
- Verify the installed herdr plugin starts (`npx tsx src/index.ts`) after build

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running `npm run build` at repo root from a clean clone installs `packages/herdr` dependencies
- [ ] `prefix+l` opens the Podcast Editing tab without the plugin crashing (pane stays alive)
- [ ] No duplicate work; existing install-herdr.sh behavior (idempotent link + keybinding insert) preserved

Discovered from: pi session 019ffb59-0480-7aff-b76f-d3bec65f7630 (SorraAgents)

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo

# Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)

## Problem

When mouse tracking is enabled in the worklist TUI (packages/herdr), the terminal sends ALL mouse events to the app, including drag events. This prevents the terminal's native text selection (click-drag to select/copy content from the terminal). Users cannot select text to copy while the worklist TUI is active, even though the TUI needs mouse support for clicking/wheel navigation.

The root cause is that SGR mouse reporting captures all mouse events from the terminal, preventing the terminal's built-in text-selection mechanism from receiving drag events.

## Root cause location

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts line 3541: mouseEnable is emitted on raw-mode entry and stays enabled for the TUI lifetime.
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts line 3560: mouseDisable is only emitted in cleanup() (TUI exit).
- Once enabled, ALL mouse events are captured, the terminal has no way to selectively receive drag events for selection.

## Solution

Add a toggle shortcut (Alt+m) that allows the user to temporarily disable mouse tracking, use the terminal's native text selection to copy content, then re-enable mouse tracking for worklist interaction.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Toggle shortcut Alt+m toggles mouse tracking on/off. Verified by unit test on the toggle key handling.
2. Toggle state tracked as boolean (mouseTrackingEnabled), initialized to true (mouse tracking enabled by default). Verified by unit test.

# Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Problem statement

During downtime dispatching through the leader, only a single audit should ever be active at any one time. The dispatch logic must check for existing active audits (dispatched but not yet completed) and skip dispatching another audit if one is already in progress, ensuring audits are strictly sequential rather than allowing fan-out.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants audit work to progress deterministically, one at a time, without competing audits consuming LLM capacity.
- **Operator relying on audit results for release decisions** — needs audit outcomes to be reliable and complete; concurrent audits increase the risk of missed findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Leader-only check** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; non-leader instances do not dispatch audits at all (unchanged behavior).
3. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for any audit-tier item (completed/in_review candidates) that has a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `audit`. If the dispatched audit entry is older than a stale threshold (2 hours), it is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier. The skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability.
5. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Audit tier only** — this constraint applies only to the audit dispatch tier; implement/plan/intake tiers are unaffected.
- **Existing single-flight guard** — the in-process `dispatchInFlight` guard remains in place; this adds a cross-idle-period guard (prevents re-dispatch on the next idle tick while a previous audit is still running).
- **Coordination file aware** — in the leader-election refactor context, the check must consider audits dispatched by any instance (not just the current instance), using the coordination file or dispatch log as the source of truth.
- **Fail-safe** — if the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the dispatcher falls through to the next tier rather than blocking all dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` dispatches audit-tier items via `dispatchClaimedTier(deps, 'audit', ...)`.
- The `dispatchInFlight` guard prevents concurrent dispatch calls within the same idle period.
- CAS claim moves dispatched items to `in_progress`, removing them from `wl next`/`wl list` selection.
- Dispatched markers in `downtime-dispatches.log` track dispatched items with kind and timestamp.
- The audit tier runs first, before implement/plan/intake tiers.
- Under the leader-election refactor (WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), only the leader dispatches, but multiple idle periods could span across a running audit.

## Desired change

1. **Active audit check** — Before selecting an audit candidate, query whether any audit-tier item is currently active (dispatched and `in_progress`). This can be done by: (a) scanning the dispatched-marker log for recent audit dispatches where the item is still `in_progress`, or (b) querying the worklog for `in_progress` items that match audit-tier criteria.
2. **Audit tier skip** — If an active audit is found, skip the audit tier and proceed to the implement tier (unchanged fallback behavior).
3. **Logging** — Log the skip reason (`audit-in-flight`) for observability.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork`: add active-audit check before `getNextAuditCandidate`; skip audit tier if active audit found; log skip reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — possibly a new dep method `getActiveAudits(cwd)` or reuse existing dispatched-marker logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests: audit skipped when one active, audit dispatched when none active, active-audit check failure falls through gracefully.

## Related work

- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** — Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file (open, plan_complete) — the primary context; this constraint applies to the leader-only dispatch model.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed) — establishes the audit tier.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed) — parent for dispatched-marker exclusion.

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (open) — directly relevant to stale-audit timeout design; a crashed audit pane that fails to update the work item state is the scenario the timeout protects against.
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed) — proxy idle/busy semantics relevant to dispatch timing.
- **WL-0ML7QRBQR183KXPB** — Auto-unblock on dependency changes (completed) — dependency resolution patterns may inform how active-audit detection handles blocked items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** An audit is considered "active" from the moment it is dispatched (marked in `downtime-dispatches.log`) until the item transitions from `in_progress` to a terminal state (`completed`/`in_review` with a fresh audit, or reverted to `completed/in_review` for re-audit).
- **Assumption:** The dispatch log or worklog query is fast enough to not impact dispatch latency (should be sub-second for typical worklog sizes).

- **Risk:** The active-audit check adds complexity to the dispatch loop. Mitigation: keep the check simple (one worklog query or log scan) and fail-open (skip audit tier on query failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extending this constraint to implement/plan/intake tiers is out of scope. Only audit-tier sequentialization is required.
- **Risk (leader-election context):** Multiple instances could have stale active-audit entries from crashed instances. Mitigation: the check should use the coordination file or dispatch log timestamps to detect stale entries.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the single-audit constraint apply only to audits, or to all dispatch tiers?" — Answer (user): "Audit only. Implement/plan/intake are not affected." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "How should we detect an 'active' audit? By worklog status or dispatch log?" — Answer (user): "Check for audit-tier items that are dispatched but not yet completed — use the dispatched markers or worklog query. The check must work in the leader-election context." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "What happens if the active-audit check fails?" — Answer (user): "Fail-open: skip the audit tier and fall through to implement. Do not block all dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Should there be a timeout on active audits? (e.g., if an audit pane crashes, the item stays in_progress forever)" — Answer (user): "Yes — add a stale-audit timeout. If an audit dispatch entry is older than a reasonable threshold (e.g., 2 hours), treat it as stale and allow re-dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Goal

Verify that every wl spawn in the herdr refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout and that a timed-out refresh recovers gracefully. Tests written first (red) against the current unbounded behavior; implementation work item WL-0MSJNJXX2001NMHS-child makes them green.

## Background

`runWl`/`runWlInner` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:339-398) pass `timeout` to execFileAsync only when the caller supplies `timeoutMs`; no refresh-path caller does. The tests below (exercised through the existing `setExecFileAsync` seam) lock in the intended bounded-spawn behavior per AC-1/AC-3 of WL-0MSJNJXX2001NMHS.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test asserts every refresh/sync-path `runWl` caller (`fetchNextItems`, `fetchItemsByStage`, `fetchItemsByPriority`, `fetchMandatorySubsets`, `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchChildrenForItem`, `runWlSync`) invokes execFileAsync with a bounded non-zero `timeout` (equal to `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, 60s, once the implementation lands) when the caller supplies no override.
- [ ] A unit test asserts explicit overrides survive: `claimItem` still passes `CLAIM_TIMEOUT_MS` (3000) rather than the default.
- [ ] A unit test asserts `checkWlAvailable` (the `wl --version` startup probe) passes a bounded timeout.
- [ ] A hung-execFile test (mock honoring `options.timeout` under fake timers) proves a fetch rejects after the timeout elapses — not before, not never.
- [ ] A worklist-level test proves the timed-out rejection surfaces the `Refresh failed` toast, clears `refreshInFlight`, and the next auto-refresh tick proceeds (no permanent wedge).
- [ ] All packages/herdr unit tests pass (no existing test depends on unbounded spawns).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts
- packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/setWorklogDir.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/claim.test.ts
